Conversion audit, Tech view

103 failing checks + 2 open questions on lhune.com

1 Critical11 High44 Medium47 Low2 questions137 pass73 unknown37 n/a

35 pages rendered (iPhone 15 Pro profile 393 x 659, DPR 2, and desktop 1440 x 900), 171 products and 1,533 variants read from the public catalog. 352 checks in catalog v2: 242 with a pass or fail from outside, 110 unknown or n/a. Theme: Dawn 15.1.0, customized (custom product, collection and footer sections). Each finding has measured values, the location, the rule, a fix and a re-check spec. Findings were re-probed independently on Oct 22, 2026 (own scripts, Chrome for Testing 151, beacons answered locally).

Rule set
check catalog v2, updated Oct 23, 2026 (352 checks: 158 original, 184 from the expert crawl, 5 first found on this store by the scanner and 5 by the re-check of the findings)

Every issue links to where it lives. Chips say where a link goes: Live page Asset Admin Test tool Docs. Admin links open nocolornewyork.myshopify.com/admin and need a staff login; paths come from Shopify Help Center links, read Oct 22, 2026. Highlight links use URL text fragments, which scroll to and mark the quoted text in Chrome 81+, Edge 83+, Safari 16.1+ and Firefox 131+ (caniuse, MDN). Theme excerpts come from the files Shopify serves, which its CDN minifies (shopify.dev), so they show the served line and column and are re-indented for reading. Repro commands are read-only; Shopify answers fast bursts with local_rate_limited, so leave a few seconds between them.

Real-user speed (CrUX field)

Real Chrome users (CrUX API), origin https://www.lhune.com, phones and computers combined, 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20, p75. Origin PHONE 404, DESKTOP 404; 0 of 8 page-level records with data. Thresholds: web.dev.

89% / 6% / 4%

Good, goodNeeds improvement, needs improvementPoor, poor

CrUX History API: 12 of 40 weekly windows had LCP data, p75 1,340 to 2,167 ms, good in every window. INP had data in 3 windows, the last ending 2026-08-01 (78 ms).

  • CrUX: opted-in Chrome on Android, Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS; excludes Chrome on iOS, Safari, Firefox, Edge and Android WebView (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux/methodology). No Safari or iOS data at all.
  • Origin-level record only, all form factors combined: origin PHONE 404, DESKTOP 404; 8 URL-level queries x 3 form factors, 0 with data. No form_factors fractions in the record, so the phone share is unknown.
  • collectionPeriod 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20 (rolling 28 days, about 2 days behind). History: weekly 28-day windows that overlap.
  • PSI Lighthouse 13.5.0: 3 runs per page and strategy, median by performance score; spread shows the range.
  • Our lab (Chrome for Testing 151, 4x CPU, Slow 4G): LCP 10,280 ms PDP, 6,180 ms home. Kept for causes only (AGENTS.md lesson, Oct 22, 2026).

Unpriced. speed-lcp-mobile-field-poor passes on field data (origin ALL p75 LCP within 2,500 ms), so its impact model (u = 2% needs-improvement to good, 8.4% poor to good) gives no band, and every cause check is sized inside it (no double count). The share of loads over 2.5 s and all Safari/iOS traffic are unmeasured from outside; connected mode adds Shopify's Web performance report (Chromium and Firefox, not Safari) and a RUM script for Safari.

Speed

3 Medium7 Low17 fine

What real shoppers see, from Google's Chrome data for Sep 23 to Oct 20, 2026: for 3 of 4 page views, the main photo or headline appeared within 1.7 seconds (Google calls up to 2.5 seconds good), the first thing on screen within 1.1 seconds, your store started sending the page within 0.63 seconds, and the page did not jump while loading. All four are in Google's good range. 89% of page views showed the main photo within 2.5 seconds; 4% took longer than 4 seconds. Looking back 40 weeks, Google had enough Chrome visits in 12 of them. Every one was in the good range: the main photo appeared within 2.0 seconds in the 28 days to Apr 18, 2026 and within 1.7 seconds in the 28 days to Oct 17, 2026. Google has no current number for how fast your pages react to a tap: not enough Chrome visits tapped in the last 28 days. The last time it had one (28 days to Aug 1, 2026), taps got a response within 0.08 seconds, which is good. Limits: this is Chrome only, so no iPhones, no Safari and no in-app browsers. It is one number for the whole site, phones and computers together; Google has no separate phone number and no number for any single page. Google's lab test, on a simulated mid-range phone with a slow connection, scored your pages 56 to 81 out of 100 for speed on Oct 22 (80 to 96 on a computer), middle of 3 runs each, and showed the main photo after 4.0 to 19.3 seconds. That test always uses the same slow phone and connection, so it runs slower than your real visits (compare the 1.7 seconds above). It also gives very different results from run to run on your pages: your home page scored anywhere from 54 to 89 across 7 runs on Oct 22. So we use it only to find causes, and our own slowed-down test (10.3 seconds on a product page) was a worst case too. In Google's test your product pages were the slowest by far: 14 to 19 seconds to show the main photo. Photos larger than the screen needs explain 15% to 49% of that time, by Google's own estimate. Google's real-user data cannot tell us whether phone shoppers on product pages feel that, which is why the photo size item keeps its grade. So the speed items below are lower priority, and none carries a dollar figure: they explain the slower page views, not a slow store.CrUX field, origin https://www.lhune.com, phone and desktop combined, 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20 (PHONE 404, DESKTOP 404; 8 URLs x 3 form factors queried, 0 with data). p75 (good / needs improvement / poor shares): LCP 1,685 ms good (89% / 6% / 4%); FCP 1,125 ms good (92% / 5% / 3%); CLS 0.00 good (96% / 1% / 2%); TTFB 628 ms good (81% / 14% / 5%); INP no record (History: last 78 ms, window ending 2026-08-01, 3 of 40 weeks with data). History API (40 weekly 28-day windows, 12 with data): LCP p75 1,340 ms to 2,167 ms, good in every window; 1,982 ms (to 2026-04-18) then 1,667 ms (to 2026-10-17). PSI v5 lab (3 runs per page and strategy, median by performance score; Lighthouse mobile: emulated Moto G Power (2022) (PSI networkUserAgent), simulated slow 4G (about 150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbps) and 4x CPU slowdown; desktop: Lighthouse desktop settings): mobile performance 56 to 81, LCP 3,976 ms to 19,256 ms (PDPs 13,726 ms to 19,256 ms; image-delivery-insight LCP savings 2,900 ms to 7,200 ms on the median runs, 15% to 49% of PDP lab LCP). Run-to-run spread: home mobile performance 54 to 89 over 7 runs (3 here, 3 in verification v5, 1 re-probe; Oct 22 US Eastern, Oct 22 to 23 UTC). Mobile TBT 40 ms to 212 ms; desktop performance 80 to 96. 16 of 16 median runs warned that the page "loaded too slowly to finish within the time limit", so late scripts can be missing from those traces. What is wrong

Your main product photos are sent at their full original size, 2,732 pixels wide, even to a phone that shows them about 350 pixels wide. Collection pages ask for each photo at 800 pixels for a tile about 180 pixels wide. In our own scan (iPhone profile), a product page downloaded about 2.4 MB of photos. In Google's lab test on a simulated slow phone (middle of 3 runs), your product pages took 14 to 19 seconds to show the main photo, and Google estimates right-sized photos would save about 7 seconds of that (2.3 MB less to download).

Why it costs sales

On a phone connection, big photos are the main reason a page feels slow to appear. Real Chrome shoppers get a fast store overall, but Google's data cannot show product pages on phones on their own, and this is where Google's lab test finds by far the biggest saving. So this is the speed fix to do first.

Not priced. Speed carries no dollar figure in this report: real Chrome shoppers already get a fast store overall (see the speed summary at the top of this area).

What to do

  1. Ask your developer to request your photos at the size the screen needs. Shopify resizes them for free. The code is in the Tech view.

Repro

Run it in the Console on Live page/products/amara-bare-brilliant-round-diamond-... (device toolbar: iPhone, 393 x 659).

How the scanner checks itFor the LCP request and first 6 images on home/PDP (emulated iPhone, DPR 3): transferSize, content-type, naturalWidth vs rendered width × DPR. Flag transfer > 200 KB, or naturalWidth > 2 × needed width, or Shopify CDN URL without width parameter, or GIF/PNG photos.

Fix

Use image_url: width: with image_tag widths and sizes (see speed-lcp-image-late-discovery). Shopify's CDN already serves WebP; adding a width makes it serve the right size. On collection cards, add widths and a sizes value matching the 177 px slot.

Repro

How the scanner checks itLighthouse 13 lcp-discovery-insight: fails when the LCP request is not discoverable from the document, lacks fetchpriority=high, or is lazy. Cross-check: LCP URL string not present in raw HTML (fetch without JS), or LCP element is a CSS background-image.

Fix

Mark the media the theme shows first, not media[0]: on the best seller the photo shown first is the third slide in the markup, and the first slide downloads in parallel at full size. The load delay in the table comes from Lighthouse's observed (unthrottled) trace, so it is far smaller than the simulated LCP; photo size (speed-hero-image-oversized) is the bigger lever.

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule speed-lcp-image-late-discovery on 2 URLs, iPhone profile. Rerun Lighthouse lcp-discovery-insight; pass when it reports discoverable + fetchpriority high.
Severity rule
high: resource load delay > 1,000 ms on PDP/home; medium: 400 to 1,000 ms; low: < 400 ms. The delay comes from Lighthouse's LCP breakdown (lcp-breakdown-insight, PSI mobile, median run). Field check: when CrUX shows a good p75 LCP for the origin or the template, drop one level (never below low) and say so; missing field data keeps the lab grade. Exception: with origin-level field data only, the lab grade stays when PSI mobile (median runs) rates at least half of the affected pages poor for that metric and attributes at least 1,000 ms of estimated savings to this cause on them.

Why it costs sales

Recording every visit costs each phone some work on every page: in Google's lab test on a simulated phone, Clarity kept the phone busy for up to 0.74 seconds on one page (middle of 3 runs). Clarity has no setting to record only some visits, so the choice is to keep it or remove it.

What to do

  1. In Clarity, check whether anyone watches the recordings. If not, turn off the Microsoft Clarity app embed in your theme editor, or remove the app.
Who
You, in Shopify admin
Effort
About 10 minutes
Fix price
Small, $99
Evidence
Measured Oct 22, 2026
Raw scan record findings.json, speed-session-replay-unsampled, trimmed

Repro

How the scanner checks itURL: in 3 fresh browser contexts, load the top PDP and the cart page in emulated iPhone and run a 10 s scripted scroll plus one variant change. Detect replay hosts (clarity.ms, hotjar, luckyorange, fullstory, contentsquare) and whether recording data is sent (requests to the vendor ingest endpoints, not only the script tag). If recording data is sent in all 3 contexts, sampling is likely off or high: at a 10% sample the chance of 3 of 3 is 0.1% (our math: 0.1 x 0.1 x 0.1). Measure Long Animation Frame time attributed to the vendor during the run. Connected: theme-file shows whether the tag is hard-coded or an app embed; the owner confirms the vendor sampling setting.

Fix

Clarity offers no sampling (Clarity FAQ). Disable the app embed if replays are unused; loading it only on chosen templates would need custom code instead of the app embed (UNVERIFIED that the app supports that).

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule speed-session-replay-unsampled on 1 URL, iPhone and desktop. Repeat the 3-context test; pass when recording data is sent only in a minority of contexts or only on the scoped templates, and recorder main-thread time drops.
Severity rule
medium: recording data sent on PDP and cart in all sampled sessions with over 100 ms of recorder main-thread time; low: sampled or scoped but still over 100 ms when active.

Repro

Run it in the Console on Live page/products/amara-bare-brilliant-round-diamond-... (device toolbar: iPhone, 393 x 659).

How the scanner checks itEmulate iPhone 13 (390x844, DPR 3) and Pixel 8; load top 2 PDPs; after load + 3 s and after closing any popup, get bounding rect of form[action*="/cart/add"] [type=submit] (or button[name=add]); flag if rect.top > innerHeight - 40. Also record whether price is above the fold. Screenshot first viewport with a red outline where the button sits below. Repeat with consent banner dismissed.

Fix

The bar shows whenever the main button is off screen and clicks the real Add to Cart, so the theme's own handler still adds the gift, lead time, custom size and certificate properties. Do not submit a form: the only /cart/add form on the page is the installments form, which would skip them. The price is copied from .price-wrapper because options change client side. Limit the bar to phones in CSS.

What is wrong

Screenshot

Why it costs sales

Shoppers who are unsure about costs or returns leave to check, and many do not come back. Saying it next to the button answers the question at the moment they decide. Baymard found 40% of people who abandon a cart do it over extra costs, and 13% over the return policy.

$480 to $1,900 a month in sales at risk, our estimate from the example numbers at the top.
Show the math

10,000 visits that view a product page a month, x 0.5% that buy, x $965 per order = $48,000 of sales a month pass through this spot. We estimate a fix wins back 1% to 4% of that: $480 to $1,900.

Our estimate, anchored on Baymard: 40% of shoppers who left a cart named extra costs, 13% the return policy.

What to do

  1. In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes and click Customize on your live theme.
  2. At the top, choose Products > Default product.
  3. In the left panel, under the product information, click Add block and choose Text. Drag it so it sits right under the Buy buttons.
  4. Type one line: "Free insured shipping. Free returns within 15 days." 15 days is your real window; your refund policy still says 30, which the returns item fixes.
  5. Click Save, then open a product page on your phone and check that the line sits right under the button.
  6. Alternative your developer can do in minutes: show that Shipping tab text by default, right under the button (see the Details and Shipping tabs item).

Your product pages use a custom product section, so the theme editor may not offer a Text block there. If you cannot find it, use "Copy for my developer" below.

Cross-check with /policies/shipping-policy and /policies/refund-policy text for contradictions (e.g. buy box says 60 days, policy says 30).

Fix

15 days, U.S. and international, is the owner's window (DD, Oct 22, 2026) and matches the approved policy text. Reuse the snippet in the cart (cart-shipping-cost-surprise).

Why it costs sales

Jewelry is often a gift with a date attached. A clear arrival date answers "will it get here in time" without a chat or an email. Without it, some shoppers buy something they can get faster.

$480 to $1,400 a month in sales at risk, our estimate from the example numbers at the top.
Show the math

10,000 visits that view a product page a month, x 0.5% that buy, x $965 per order = $48,000 of sales a month pass through this spot. We estimate a fix wins back 1% to 3% of that: $480 to $1,400.

Our estimate. Shopify's own delivery-promise figures are vendor claims, so we do not use them.

What to do

  1. Decide your honest range: your shipping policy says up to 15 days to make plus 2 to 4 days to deliver, and in-stock pieces go out within 7 days by 2-day shipping.
  2. Ask your developer to show a date range under the "Made to order" line, for example "Arrives Nov 8 to Nov 16 if you order today". Your gift option already works out dates, so the developer can reuse that. The code is in the Tech view.
  3. Before each gifting date, add an order-by line (see the dates in Summary).

How the scanner checks itSearch the buy box text for a date pattern (weekday/month/day, "arrives", "get it by", "delivery by") or a Shop Promise badge element; LLM fallback classifier on the buy box text. Flag "ships in 3-5 days" style text as partial.

Fix

Reuses the drawer's own today(), addDays() and fmtDate() (store time zone America/New_York) instead of a second date calculation. The dates are worked out in the browser, so cached pages stay right.

Made to order: 15 to 21 days to make plus 2 to 4 in transit (17 to 25). In stock: up to 7 days to process plus 2-day shipping (our estimate, 3 to 9). The gift note stops saying "made to order" on in-stock pieces.

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule pdp-delivery-date-missing on 14 URLs, iPhone profile. Reload PDP; pass when a date range renders in the buy box and its dates match settings for a simulated "now".
Severity rule
high: no delivery info at all near ATC from Nov 1 to Dec 20; medium: speed only, no date; low: date present but no cutoff time.

How the scanner checks itFetch /policies/refund-policy. An LLM with a strict schema extracts the return window in days, exclusions (final sale, clearance, sale items, custom, personalized, engraved, resized, intimates, gift cards), fees (restocking, engraving removal) and resize terms. Sample PDPs that fall under each exclusion (tags or collections named sale, clearance or final; products with an engraving or personalization option; on-sale variants). Within 400 px of the ATC on mobile look for text matching final sale, non-returnable, no returns, exchange only or the excluded condition. Why it costs sales

Surprise costs are the top reason people abandon a cart (40% in Baymard's survey). Here there is no cost, only the fear of one. One sentence fixes it.

$970 to $2,900 a month in sales at risk, our estimate from the example numbers at the top.
Show the math

20,000 visits a month, x 0.5% that buy, x $965 per order = $97,000 of sales a month pass through this spot. We estimate a fix wins back 1% to 3% of that: $970 to $2,900.

Our estimate, applied to all sales because every order passes the cart. Lower than the catalog band because your shipping is free: the cost is doubt, not a fee.

What to do

  1. In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes, click the three dots next to your live theme, and choose Edit default theme content.
  2. Search for "calculated at checkout". Several lines match: edit the one that starts "Taxes, discounts and".
  3. Change it to: "Free insured shipping. Free returns within 15 days. Taxes calculated at checkout." Save.
  4. Open your cart on a phone and check the new line.

This one line also answers the checkout reassurance item: nothing near Check out says why to buy from you today.

Edit default theme content (no code), or override the key in locales/en.default.json: "taxes_at_checkout_shipping_at_checkout_with_policy_html": "Free insured <a href=\"{{ link }}\">shipping</a>. Free returns within 15 days. Taxes calculated at checkout."

Shopify fills that list from the countries your shipping settings cover (our reading of Shopify's own documentation). If your settings really cover only the US, a shopper in Canada or the UK can fill a cart and then find no way to ship at checkout.

Why it matters

Shopify Help: customers outside every zone see that no shipping rate is available for their region. Shopify changelog (Mar 7, 2023): buyers can only check out if their country or region is in an active market. Current Markets docs say unmatched customers get the backup region's experience; how checkout treats them in the 2026 admin is UNVERIFIED.

Owner fact (DD, Oct 22, 2026): LHUNE ships internationally. /meta.json is public and undocumented; its field matches Admin GraphQL Shop.shipsToCountries ("The list of countries that the shop ships to"). Why it costs sales

Shoppers check how hard a return is before a big purchase. "Start a return in two taps" sounds easier than "email us". It also saves you the back-and-forth.

Not priced. Mostly support time saved; we show it, we do not add it to sales.

What to do

  1. Settings > Customer accounts: turn on "Self-serve returns and cancellations", and pick "Return requests only" if you do not want cancel requests.
  2. Settings > Policies > Return and cancellation rules: set a 15-day window, free return shipping, and custom or engraved pieces as final sale.
  3. Shopify can fill your refund policy's return terms from these rules. After saving, check that the approved returns text from the policy item is still there word for word.
  4. Once self-serve returns are on, tell us and we will draft one added sentence for both pages ("Start a return from your account, or email hello@LHUNE.com.") for you to approve. The approved text fixes the old address; the shipping policy line needs the real address too.

Why it costs sales

Shoppers who did not notice the tick end up on your list, unsubscribe or mark you as spam. In the EU and UK, a pre-ticked box is not valid consent.

Not priced. Consent risk. We never put a dollar figure on it.

What to do

  1. Settings > Checkout > Marketing opt-in > Email. Look at which regions start with the box ticked: "Regions recommended by Shopify" or "Regions you choose".
  2. To never pre-tick it, choose "Regions you choose", click Edit, select no regions, and save. Or keep it only for the US, and review it before you sell to the EU or UK.

Our estimate. Shoppers who check returns before a big purchase find two answers.

What to do

  1. Settings > Policies > Refund policy: replace the whole text with the text below, then Save.
  2. Online Store > Pages > Return & Exchanges: paste the same text, then Save. Use it word for word on both pages:
    We're only happy if you're happy. If you're not completely satisfied with your purchase, we offer a no-questions-asked refund within 15 days of receiving your item, as long as it's in its original condition. Customized or engraved pieces are final sale. Returns are hassle-free and include free shipping, in the U.S. and internationally. Just email us at hello@LHUNE.com with your order number, and we'll send you a free return label. For international orders, duties and taxes paid on delivery are set by your country and are not refunded by LHUNE.
  3. This also changes the old hello@nocolornyc.com email to hello@LHUNE.com on the refund policy.
  4. Optional, same visit: change the return line near Add to Cart to "Free returns within 15 days, U.S. and international."
  5. Optional, same visit: change "Complimentary shipping on all purchases in the US" (product pages and home page) to "Complimentary insured shipping, in the U.S. and internationally."
  6. Tap "I did it" and we compare every page again.

Why it costs sales

The FTC's Jewelry Guides ask that a lab-grown stone's name be "immediately preceded with equal conspicuousness" by "laboratory-grown" or a similar word. A title is often all a shopper sees in search results. This is our reading of the rule, not legal advice.

Not priced. Legal risk. We never put a dollar figure on it.

What to do

  1. Products > each product > Search engine listing > Page title: put "Lab-Grown" right before "Diamond", for example "Amara Bare Round Lab-Grown Diamond Tennis Bracelet".
  2. Do the same in the 8 product titles that say "Diamond" alone.
  3. For image descriptions, we can fix all 220 at once from a list you approve (see the alt text item).
  4. In your FAQ, change "Lab-grown diamonds are real diamonds" to "Lab-grown diamonds are diamonds: chemically, physically and optically the same as mined diamonds."
  5. On product pages, change FAQ 05 to "Are your diamonds lab-grown? Yes. They are diamonds: chemically, physically and optically the same as mined diamonds."
  6. Ask your lawyer to confirm the wording.

Classify products as lab-grown from tags, product_type, body_html and handle (lab, lab-grown, lab grown, lgd, cvd, hpht). For each, tokenize the title, image alt text, the PDP h1, meta title and JSON-LD name, and flag any "diamond" whose 3 preceding words lack lab-grown, laboratory-grown, lab-created, laboratory-created or a maker name followed by created. Render the PDP at 390x844 and check the qualifier is visible in the first viewport near the h1; flag "qualifier only in the description or FAQ" separately. Screen all product text, collection descriptions and meta descriptions for: real, genuine, natural or precious next to lab-grown stones; "cultured diamond" with no lab qualifier within 5 words; moissanite, cubic zirconia or simulant within 40 characters of "diamond"; and the abbreviation LGD. Flag mixed vocabulary across the store. Output each hit with its URL and sentence for review.

Repro

How the scanner checks itCollect the text of every /pages/* page whose handle or title mentions certification, grading, IGI, GIA, quality, diamond, about or FAQ, plus the spec lines and FAQ blocks on sampled PDPs (rendered). Extract grade claims with fixed patterns, not a language model, so the result repeats: color letters on GIA's D to Z scale as one grade or a range ("D color", "D-F", "D, E, or F"), clarity on GIA's scale (FL, IF, VVS1, VVS2, VS1, VS2, SI1, SI2, I1 to I3, plus store shorthand such as "VVS" or "VS+"), and certification scope ("every stone", "all diamonds", "over 0.3 ct"). Map each claim to a range on the scale. Flag a store-wide claim ("our stones are", "every stone", "across the board") whose range is narrower or better than the range a PDP states for the same stone type, and a claim that every stone is certified next to one that limits certification. Quote each source. Scanner rule not written yet: an independent verifier found this on LHUNE (2026-10-22), so a scan reports the check as unknown until the rule exists.

Fix

Edit the two "LHUNE stones are graded" sentences and the "Every stone independently verified" line on /pages/igi-certification; keep the page's own "Color: D, E, or F" and "Clarity: VVS-VS" consistent with the PDP spec lines.

How the scanner checks itURL: in PDP text and spec tables find grade patterns: a color letter D to M near a clarity grade (FL, IF, VVS1, VVS2, VS1, VS2, SI1, SI2, I1), cut grades (Excellent, Ideal), or Premium or Standard next to GIA. When found, require a lab name in the same block (GIA, IGI, GCAL, HRD) and a report number pattern (IGI LG followed by 6 to 12 digits, GIA 9 to 10 digits) or a link to the igi.org or gia.edu report check. On pages that mention GIA and lab-grown together, flag GIA with a D to Z color or clarity grade as a review item, since older GIA lab-grown reports remain valid. Connected: read product and variant metafields for certificate lab, number and file; flag products with grades and empty certificate fields.

Link to IGI's report check without prefilling: the prefill URL format is UNVERIFIED and IGI's check asks for the report number and the carat weight. Confirm the current report-check address on igi.org before shipping.

Tracking and ads

1 Critical1 High1 Medium2 Low10 fine

Redirects keep your ad click codes, Google Analytics counts one page view per normal visit, and Meta gets one Add to Cart per add. The serious problem: your product pages wipe the ad click code as they load, so Google and Meta cannot link those clicks to later sales. Your OpenAI ad tracking also keeps running when a shopper opts out of data sharing, while your other ad tools stop. Whether every sale reaches Google and Meta needs your store connected.Pass: click IDs and UTMs survive HTTP redirects and the home and collection landings (_gcl_aw, _fbc set); GA4 one page_view per normal load; Meta AddToCart once per add. Fail: PDP replaceState drops gclid, fbclid, ttclid and utm_* before tags read them (8 of 8 PDP loads in verification v4); GPC honored by Meta, Pinterest, Reddit, Clarity and Google (rdp=1, npa=1) but not by the OpenAI custom pixel; ShopMy landings fire a second page_view. Purchase capture rate needs read_orders plus GA4 and Meta access.

26 Your product pages erase the ad click code before Google and Meta can read itTheme replaceState on PDP load drops gclid, fbclid, ttclid and utm_* before tags read them CriticalOpenYour developerAbout an hourFix $99 track-click-id-strippedCriticalOpenTracking and ads1 pageAbout an hourassets/no-color-v2.js:1:2710

What is wrong

When a shopper taps one of your ads, the link carries a click code (and tags like "source: Instagram"). Your home page and collection pages keep them. Your product pages do not: about half a second after a product page opens, your theme rewrites the address to add the chosen option, and the click code and tags are wiped before Google and Meta read them. Google Ads and Meta still see the ad click, but they cannot link it to a later sale, and Google Analytics usually records the visit with no source. Shopify's own reports still see the tags.

Where

Every product page, which is where Google Shopping ads and most Meta product ads send people.

Why it costs sales

Google Ads and Meta learn which ads sell by matching the click to the sale. When the click code is gone, sales from product page ads look like they came from nowhere, so the platforms spend your budget on the wrong ads and your reports undercount what works.

Not priced. This costs ad money more than sales: Google and Meta bid on incomplete data. Ad spend is never added to the sales figure, and pricing it needs your ad spend.

What to do

  1. Ask your developer to change one line in your theme so the address keeps everything already in it when the option is added. The exact change is in the Tech view.
  2. Then open the test link your developer sends you (a product link with a test click code added), wait a few seconds, and check the address still shows the code. Do not tap your own paid ads to test it: each tap costs you a click.
  3. Tap "I did it" and we repeat the test with ad click codes on a product page.
Who
Your developer
Effort
About an hour
Fix price
Small, $99
Evidence
Measured Oct 22, 2026
Raw scan record findings.json, track-click-id-stripped, trimmed

Repro

Run it in the Console on Live page/products/amara-bare-brilliant-round-diamond-... (device toolbar: iPhone, 393 x 659).

How the scanner checks itRequest the homepage, top PDP and any ad URLs supplied, each with ?utm_source=fixlane&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=fixlane_test&gclid=FIXLANETEST123&fbclid=FIXLANETEST123&ttclid=FIXLANETEST123 (the query the scanner sends). Follow HTTP redirects (log each hop) and wait 6 s for JS redirects. Compare final location.search with the input. Also check that _gcl_aw / _fbc cookies are set when Google/Meta tags are present. Repeat from a non-US egress to trigger geo redirects. Report the exact hop that drops parameters.

Fix

The current code builds the URL from the path and the variant only. Building it from window.location keeps the ad parameters; tags that load later still read them. Keep a guard so replaceState runs only when the URL changes: if (url.href !== window.location.href) window.history.replaceState({}, '', url.toString()). The fix also stops ShopMy re-adding smsclickid after the strip, which today fires a second GA4 page_view and a second Meta PageView on affiliate landings (adhoc-shopmy-landing-double-pageview).

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule track-click-id-stripped on 1 URL, iPhone and desktop. Re-run the same tagged URLs; pass when all parameters survive to the final URL and the vendor cookies are set.
Pass when
PDP final URL keeps gclid, fbclid, ttclid and utm_*; _gcl_aw and _fbc set; GA4 page_view dl carries the UTMs.
Severity rule
critical: click IDs dropped on the homepage or any ad landing URL; high: UTMs kept but gclid/fbclid dropped; medium: dropped only for one market redirect.

What to do

Repro

How the scanner checks itFrom a US egress in a state Shopify covers (for example California), load home and a PDP twice: once normally and once with Global Privacy Control on (navigator.globalPrivacyControl set to true by an init script, plus the Sec-GPC: 1 header). No form is touched. In the GPC run, load the Customer Privacy API with Shopify.loadFeatures and read window.Shopify.customerPrivacy.saleOfDataAllowed(); capture marketing hits with beacons answered locally (204). Flag vendors that fire unchanged in the GPC run: facebook.com/tr without data processing options (dpo=LDU), Pinterest events without opt_out, Google Ads hits without restricted data processing. Also flag stores that sell to the US with no data sale opt-out link (decision for the owner and counsel).

Fix

Customer events > OpenAI pixel: set the pixel's customer privacy permission to require marketing permission and to count as data sale, so Shopify blocks it when saleOfDataAllowed is false (setting labels UNVERIFIED for the 2026 admin). Or, in the pixel code, return early when the customer privacy API reports that sale of data is not allowed.

How the scanner checks itWhen the app inventory shows ShopMy (static.shopmy.us), open the top PDP on the iPhone profile with ?smsclickid=FIXLANETEST123 (the scanner's test code), beacons answered locally. Log every history.pushState and replaceState call with its time and caller, and count GA4 page_view and Meta PageView hits for the one landing. Fail when the landing sends more than one of either and a history call sits between them. Record whether ShopMy still sent its click (confirm_click request, sms_click_id cookie). Scanner rule not written yet: an independent verifier found this on LHUNE (2026-10-22), so a scan reports the check as unknown until the rule exists.

Fix

Same change as track-click-id-stripped: build the URL from window.location so the query string stays; ShopMy then has nothing to re-add and no history-change page views fire.

Why it costs sales

If shoppers cannot read the options, they do not know a 3 or 4 carat exists. It also makes the store harder to use for people with weaker eyesight, which is a legal risk for online stores in the US.

$97 to $480 a month in sales at risk, our estimate from the example numbers at the top.
Show the math

10,000 visits that view a product page a month, x 0.5% that buy, x $965 per order = $48,000 of sales a month pass through this spot. We estimate a fix wins back 0.2% to 1% of that: $97 to $480.

Our estimate for faint choices on the buy box. Accessibility legal risk is not priced.

What to do

  1. Ask your developer to darken the grey used for unselected choices. The exact color is in the Tech view.
  2. For the chat button, pick a darker button color in the Shopify Inbox settings, one that white text reads well on.

Repro

How the scanner checks itPlaywright keyboard-only script on the top PDP at 1280x800: Tab from page start; record focus order and whether each focused element shows a visible indicator (outline or box-shadow differs from the unfocused computed style); reach each option group and choose a value with Space or arrow keys; reach the add-to-cart button. Connected stores and LHUNE only: press Enter on add to cart, confirm focus moves into the drawer or a confirmation, change quantity by keyboard, Tab to Check out and stop before checkout loads. On other stores URL mode stops at add-to-cart focus (no add to cart). Log the first failing step. Fixes live in a11y-variant-picker-semantics and a11y-focus-modals; this check reports the flow.

Fix

The theme hides the radios with display: none, which removes them from the tab order; a rule that only sets opacity and size keeps that display: none. no-color-v2.js already binds $(".variant-option input[type='radio']").on("change", handleVariantSelection), so arrow keys will change the variant once the radios can take focus.

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule a11y-keyboard-purchase-path on 1 URL, desktop 1440 x 900. Rerun the keyboard flow; pass when every step completes and focus is visible throughout.
Severity rule

How the scanner checks itFind slideshow components in the first two viewports (slideshow-component, swiper, splide, flickity, slick, [data-autoplay], auto-rotate settings in section JSON). At 390 px, record the active slide (aria-current, aria-hidden or transform) at 0 s and after 12 s without input; any change is a mobile autorotation finding. At 1440 px, measure the interval (flag under 5 s), then hover and focus inside the carousel and confirm rotation stops. Look for a button whose accessible name contains pause, stop or play. For autoplay video, check muted and a pause control. Compare each slide link target with the other links on the page and flag slides whose destination appears nowhere else.

Fix

Change only the autoplay option and keep the others (loop, arrows, progress dots). If autoplay stays, add a button that calls slider.autoplay.stop() and start().

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule a11y-autoplay-carousel on 1 URL, iPhone and desktop. Repeat the 12 s observation at 390 px and the interval and hover test at 1440 px.

medium: auto-rotation with no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2, Level A); medium: auto-rotation on phones; low: desktop interval under 5 s with a pause control; low: slide destinations not linked elsewhere.

Repro

How the scanner checks itRun axe-core on each rendered collection page (iPhone and desktop). Keep the aria-allowed-attr, list and target-size results whose targets sit inside product cards. Record the selector, node count, the attribute and the rendered size of one swatch. Cross-check PSI mobile accessibility on the same collection URLs for the same audits. Scanner rule not written yet: an independent verifier found this on LHUNE (2026-10-22), so a scan reports the check as unknown until the rule exists.

Fix

Replace aria-selected with aria-pressed, move the <p> label into its own li (or out of the list), and give each button at least 24 x 24 px (min-width and min-height: 24px). The family loop stands for however the section lists the metals today.

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule a11y-collection-swatch-aria on 1 URL, iPhone profile. Run axe on the same collection pages; pass when aria-allowed-attr and list report 0 nodes inside product cards and every swatch target is at least 24 x 24 CSS px.
Pass when
axe aria-allowed-attr 0 and list 0 on /collections/all-jewelry; swatch targets at least 24 x 24 px.

medium: an ARIA attribute the role does not allow (axe aria-allowed-attr) on swatch or other card controls; low: only list structure or target size on the tiles.

Flag legibility when the rendered text cap height at 390 px is under 12 CSS px (our threshold).

Fix

Render the slide text as HTML over or beside the image, or copy it into the alt attribute.

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule a11y-text-in-images on 1 URL, iPhone and desktop. Re-run OCR on the replaced banners.

medium: offer details (discount, code, dates) exist only inside an image; low: slogans only.

Why it matters

Rule seo-robots-custom-drops-defaults. The catalog rule says medium when a Googlebot or Bingbot group reopens checkout, cart, search or filter URLs; graded low here because search is noindex, sort and filter URLs canonicalize and the catalog is small (verification v4; the catalog owner confirms). Google: "User agent specific groups and global groups (*) are not combined." (spec updated Aug 31, 2026, read Oct 22). RFC 9309 section 2.2.1. Shopify Help: "If you want to use the default robots.txt file again, then you can delete your custom robots.txt.liquid file."

The file is an old pasted copy (header "# we use Shopify as our ecommerce platform", Sitemap on nocolornyc.com); Shopify's current generated robots.txt (seen Oct 22 on theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com, brooklinen.com and tentree.com) has a new header and no /policies/ or /search block. Raw scan record findings.json, seo-robots-custom-drops-defaults, trimmed

Repro

How the scanner checks itGET /robots.txt. Parse groups per RFC 9309 (merge duplicate groups for one agent; never merge a named group with *). For each named group of a search or AI crawler, test sample paths with Google longest-match rules: /checkout, /cart, /account, /search?q=x, /collections/all?sort_by=price-ascending, /collections/all?filter.v.price.gte=1&filter.v.price.lte=2. Flag a path the * group blocks and a named group allows. Also flag a * group missing most Shopify default lines (for example Disallow: /checkouts/, /cart, /collections/*sort_by*, */collections/*filter*&*filter*), the sign of a template that does not loop robots.default_groups.

Fix

Delete templates/robots.txt.liquid (Online Store > Themes > Edit code), then confirm /robots.txt shows Shopify's generated header and Sitemap: https://www.lhune.com/sitemap.xml. This also fixes seo-robots-sitemap-host and seo-policies-blocked-by-robots.

shopify.dev warns that rendered template output does not always match Shopify's generated file exactly: compare the output with a stock store first.

Acceptance

medium: a Googlebot or Bingbot group reopens checkout, cart, search or filter URLs; low: an AI crawler group does the same; low: default lines missing from the * group.

How the scanner checks itCluster /products.json titles by stem (e.g. "Tee - Black", "Tee - White") and flag a cluster only when its members are true variants of one item (size, color, material) with the same description. Who

Effort

Fix price

Evidence

Raw scan record findings.json, mobile-overlay-covers-atc, trimmed

Repro

Run it in the Console on Live page/cart (device toolbar: iPhone, 393 x 659).

How the scanner checks itEmulated iPhone, PDP, after 8 s (widgets load late) and after scrolling (sticky bar visible): for the ATC and sticky ATC, sample 5 points (center and corners inset 4 px) with document.elementFromPoint; flag if the hit element is not the button or its descendant. Identify the overlay by id/class/iframe src (gorgias, tidio, shopify inbox, klaviyo teaser, userway, accessibe, cookie banners). Repeat on the cart page or open drawer with one item (only where the scan may add to cart: the owner asked for the audit) for the checkout button and the accelerated checkout row. Launchers inside shadow DOM (Shopify Inbox) return their host element to elementFromPoint, so take their box with a shadow-piercing locator and intersect it with each button. Screenshot with the overlap highlighted.

Fix

body.template-cart is on the live /cart page. shopify-chat is the launcher's light-DOM host, so hiding the host hides the launcher; !important beats the shadow root's :host rules (UNVERIFIED that Shopify Inbox never re-shows it). kl-teaser-Wyua8F is the class Klaviyo gave this form's teaser on Oct 22: confirm it before shipping. Alternative for the teaser: add /cart to the form's URL exclusions in Klaviyo (whether the teaser follows it is UNVERIFIED). Test on a phone.

Acceptance

Re-run
Rule mobile-overlay-covers-atc on 1 URL, iPhone profile. Repeat elementFromPoint sampling after 8 s and on scroll; pass when all sampled points hit the button.
Severity rule
critical: center point of ATC covered; high: sticky ATC covered, > 30% of button area covered, or the center of the cart checkout or a wallet button covered; medium: overlay covers price or variant picker, or part of the cart checkout or wallet buttons.

Why it costs sales

Shoppers who are unsure of the size either leave, or buy, guess wrong and send it back. A simple guide (how to measure at home, a printable sizer, and your resizing policy) keeps them on the page.

$120 to $480 a month in sales at risk, our estimate from the example numbers at the top.
Show the math

Our estimate: the catalog band (1% to 4% of sessions on sized product pages) times 44 of 171 products that have a Ring Size option.

What to do

  1. Write a short ring size guide: how to measure a finger with a strip of paper, a size chart, and what happens if the size is wrong (resize or exchange).
  2. In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Pages > Add page, call it "Ring size guide" and paste it in.
  3. Ask your developer to show the same "Size guide" link that bracelets have next to Ring Size, opening this guide.
  4. Add one line under the sizes, for example "Not sure of the size? We resize. Email hello@LHUNE.com." Say "free" only if resizing is free.

Which pieces keep selling when out of stock (right for made-to-order), and whether every one of them says so on the page with a date.bfcm-oversell-policy, bfcm-inventory-cover-low (production capacity for made-to-order), pdp-stock-message-mismatch.
Access you would grantAccess
Read access to products and inventory.read_products, read_inventory.
What we could then fixWhat we can stage or push
We give you the list; stock settings are yours.Not pushed.

You approve every change before it goes live. We never publish your theme, install apps, or touch payments, domains or your Google and Meta accounts.Theme fixes ship to an unpublished theme (`shopify theme push --unpublished`), never `--publish`. Data writes use optional scopes granted per fix, with the old value stored for rollback. Two scopes need protected customer data approval: read_orders (level 1) and read_reports (level 2).

What we checked

137 things you got right. And what we could not see.137 passing checks, 110 not evaluated.

A report that only lists problems hides what is fine. This is everything that passed, then everything we could not check and why.pass: rule evaluated with no failing condition. unknown: needs access or a run we did not do. n/a: rule does not apply to this store.

Checked and found finePassing checks

Speed

  • Real Chrome shoppers see your main photo quickly: within 1.7 seconds for 3 of 4 page views, inside Google's good line of 2.5 seconds. This is one number for phones and computers together.CrUX field, origin https://www.lhune.com, phone and desktop combined, 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20: LCP p75 1,685 ms (good); 11% of loads over 2,500 ms. No PHONE or URL-level record (404). Phone p75 could exceed 2.5 s only if desktop were over 58% of Chrome loads and all good (our estimate: (0.894 - 0.75) / 0.25).
  • For real Chrome shoppers, your pages do not jump while they load.CrUX field, origin https://www.lhune.com, phone and desktop combined, 2026-09-23 to 2026-10-20: CLS p75 0.00 (good); 2% of loads over 0.25.
  • Your Tag Manager container itself is not oversized.GTM container size and tag count under the rule threshold (duplicates are a separate finding).
  • Tapping Back shows the previous page instantly.Collection to PDP and back, and PDP to /cart and back, restored from the back/forward cache (no blocking reasons). Tested with the cache really on: Playwright's default launch passes --disable-back-forward-cache.
  • Shopify's "load the next page early" feature is on and nothing fights it.Speculation-Rules header present; no competing prefetch library.
  • Your collection photos come in sizes for phones.Product tiles carry srcset; the two images the scan flagged are decorative corner icons (top-left.png, top-right.png, about 9 KB) and not oversized at 2x. The 800 px tile requests are part of speed-hero-image-oversized.
  • No heavy autoplay video on your first screens.No autoplay video or video iframe in the first viewport of home or PDPs.
  • No A/B testing tool hides your pages while they load.No page-hiding style or testing vendor script in the raw HTML of 30 pages; no testing vendor host requested.
  • Your main photos appear as soon as they arrive; nothing fades them in late.LCP renderTime minus loadTime under 100 ms on home and 4 PDPs; no reveal classes on the LCP image chain.
  • Your sign-up pop-up does not count as the page's main content in Google's speed measure.Last LCP entry is page content on home and PDPs; the Klaviyo form opens about 3 to 5 s after load (3 s delay plus a 20% scroll, or on short pages without one) and does not produce a later LCP entry.
  • Phones download one home page banner, not the desktop one too.Home first section: one hero img on iPhone (fetchpriority high, eager); no hidden copy downloaded.
  • Your pages do not waste early connections.Preconnects to api.config-security.com and conf.config-security.com belong to Triple Whale (app block triple_pixel_snippet) and are used in the first seconds; shop.app and monorail are used. Only Judge.me's 3 dns-prefetch lines (printed by its judgeme_core app block) go unused: a DNS lookup each, nothing the theme can edit.
  • Your pages can start arriving before Shopify has finished building them.JSON templates on home, collection and PDP; content_for_header in head. Base CSS after it is Dawn's order and is preloaded by Shopify.
  • Visitors reach Shopify directly, with no extra service in between.www.lhune.com CNAME shops.myshopify.com; one cf-ray, Server-Timing intact, no via, age or x-cache headers. Cloudflare nameservers noted (zone exists, not proxying).
  • No "speed booster" fakes your test scores.No test-tool sniffing or API patching in the HTML or 45 theme files; a Lighthouse user agent got the same page (167 vs 184 scripts, within 20%).
  • Your chat button loads lightly until someone uses it.Chat (Shopify Inbox) bytes before interaction under 150 KB on the PDP; no off-screen video or map frames.
  • Nothing slides in during load and pushes the page around.No layout-property animation running during load; header transitions exist in CSS but did not run.

Mobile

  • Email and phone boxes bring up the right keyboard.Input types and autocomplete correct on capture and login forms.
  • Categories are two taps away in the phone menu.Menu depth within the rule threshold (18 links on first open).
  • Tapping Back on a phone leaves the page, with no pop-up trap.No pushState calls; the theme uses replaceState for ?variant= only. One Back left the PDP.
  • Visitors do not get several pop-ups in a row.At most one capture dialog per page.
  • Once closed, your pop-up stays away for 5 days.After closing, no dialog on / or /collections/all-jewelry (probes.json teasers); Klaviyo form config COOKIE_TIMEOUT 5.

  • After shoppers close your pop-up, a small round % button stays in the corner so they can open the offer again.Klaviyo teaser (CIRCLE, bottom left, icon only, no text) on the next pages after closing the form, /cart included (where it covers part of Shop Pay: mobile-overlay-covers-atc).
  • Your sign-up form asks for one thing: an email.One email input and a 48 px button (input font size is mobile-input-zoom-ios).
  • Your pop-up's way out is a plain close button, with no guilt line.Decline control: "Close dialog".
  • Your forms do not ask shoppers to type things twice or block pasting.No confirm-email or confirm-password fields; no disabled submit at load.

Product pages

  • No product page opens on a sold-out option.Default variant available on all sampled PDPs.

  • Choices are shown as buttons, not hidden in drop-downs.No select-based pickers.
  • The price is clear and on the first screen.Price above the fold on 14/14 PDPs; one price, no conflicting compare-at.

  • You have a comparison page that explains your options.Comparison content exists and answers 200 (re-probed Oct 22, 2026: /pages/classic-and-bare-tennis-bracelet-comparison and /blogs/lhune/amara-vs-amara-bare-what-s-actually-different). Linked from 1 of 16 PDPs (Amara Bare, Weight option header); other look-alike clusters (Ciel full vs half pave, Virelle emerald-cut vs east-west, Amara Petite vs Round) have no comparison link (a test idea).
  • No upsell box pushes the button down.No upsell widget between price and ATC.
  • Gift buyers can mark an order as a gift and add an occasion."This is a gift" and "Add occasion & date" in the buy box; gift card product exists.

  • Your Add to Cart is a strong, dark button that stands out.ATC fill rgb(65,64,66) on #fbf6ee: 9.58:1; label 10.31:1; no stronger button in the buy box.
  • Shoppers can tell there are more photos to see.Mobile gallery shows the next slide peeking in; desktop shows all photos stacked.
  • Shoppers looking at your most expensive pieces can reach a person.Visible Live chat launcher on every PDP. The "Here to help" block with hello@LHUNE.com near the top is in the page but clipped out of view on the iPhone profile, so only chat counts.
  • Your sizes and specs are written as text, not only in pictures.Size guides are text tables; carat, color, clarity and metal are page text.
  • Made-to-order pieces say how long they take, right by the button."Made to order, 2-3 weeks for production" near the ATC; full price at checkout, no deposit. Arrival date is pdp-delivery-date-missing.
  • Every combination of options you show can actually be bought.All option combinations exist as variants on the top products (option grid from /products/<handle>.js).

  • The search suggestions never come up empty for things you sell.22 catalog queries against /search/suggest.json, 0 empty; real catalog terms rank their matches first. It passes partly because search never returns zero for anything (nav-search-ignores-query).

Cart and checkout

  • Add to Cart works: the piece lands in the cart./cart/add.js 200, cart 0 to 1. The full cart page load is cart-atc-redirects-to-cart.

Tracking and ads

  • Google and Meta are set up to receive your sales.Google & YouTube pixel sends purchase; Facebook & Instagram pixel installed (capture rate needs connection).
  • Meta does not count your normal visits twice.One Meta PageView and one ViewContent per load when facebook.com/tr is answered like Meta does (200 GIF). With a 204 answer the pixel retries about 5 s later; that resend is a scan artifact, and Meta does not deduplicate two browser events with the same eventID. Exception: ShopMy affiliate landings (adhoc-shopmy-landing-double-pageview).
  • Google Analytics counts one page view per normal visit.One GA4 page_view per load with beacons answered 204, one measurement ID (G-1DX8K9CLV0), on home, collection and 8 PDP loads (verification v4). Exception: ShopMy-tagged PDP landings (adhoc-shopmy-landing-double-pageview).
  • Google Ads is set up to hear about purchases.Purchase event with an AW- send_to configured (recording status needs Google Ads access).
  • Your own links do not carry ad tags.0 internal links with utm_ parameters.
  • No old, dead tracking tools load.No Universal Analytics or other sunset tags.
  • The number of tracking tools is within normal range.Pixel count under the rule threshold (weight is a separate finding).
  • Google Ads purchases are tied to your order numbers.The only Google Ads purchase conversion is the Google & YouTube app's, sent with the order id; none in GTM or custom pixels.
  • No tools try to identify anonymous visitors.No identity resolution vendor hosts in any request.
  • Google Analytics records what shoppers search for.GA4 view_search_results and search events on /search.
